name: Xanthoria parietina / Caloplaca marina — the orange maritime lichens

represent.shader: level.js: the orange band in the granite branch reads uCover.r as its amount; rosettes from the fine noise

confidence: medium: zonation and substrate from the shore-ecology literature; the sun and wetness curves are the naturalist's calibration

sources.cite: Brodo, I.M., Sharnoff, S.D. & Sharnoff, S. (2001) Lichens of North America. Yale University Press.
sources.note: X. parietina on nutrient-enriched sunlit rock, especially near the sea and bird perches; orange foliose rosettes

sources.cite: Stephenson, T.A. & Stephenson, A. (1949) The universal features of zonation between tide-marks on rocky coasts. Journal of Ecology 37: 289–305.
sources.note: the orange (Xanthoria/Caloplaca) belt lies above the black (Verrucaria) belt in the supralittoral, below the grey crustose lichens

sources.cite: Lewis, J.R. (1964) The Ecology of Rocky Shores. English Universities Press.
sources.note: the supralittoral fringe widens with exposure: the orange belt reaches higher on exposed headlands than in sheltered bays (the salt field)

sources.cite: Fletcher, A. (1973) The ecology of maritime (supralittoral) lichens on some rocky shores of Anglesey. Lichenologist 5: 401–422.
sources.note: distribution of the orange supralittoral species against spray, aspect and nutrient enrichment
